items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique.

Since 2021, Project Zero has followed a “90 + 30” vulnerability disclosure policy, allowing vendors up to 90 days to remediate a vulnerability plus an extra 30 days “soak time” for patch rollout. Our goal was to encourage faster patching and give vendors time to deliver patches to users.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique.

Since 2021, Project Zero has followed a “90 + 30” vulnerability disclosure policy, allowing vendors up to 90 days to remediate a vulnerability plus an extra 30 days “soak time” for patch rollout. Our goal was to encourage faster patching and give vendors time to deliver patches to users. The advent of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation has changed the threat landscape such that the vulnerability remediation timeline encouraged by our disclosure policy is clearly insufficient. LLMs have increased the speed at which attackers can find and exploit vulnerabilities, alongside the risk that multiple parties, including malicious ones, discover the same bug. A vulnerability reported today presents a much higher immediate risk to users than one reported last year. In this new environment, it is crucial that vendors move towards remediating vulnerabilities faster. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Osaka, Japan's third-largest city, told its 2.8 million residents to be wary of suspicious emails purporting to come from the local government.

The city of Osaka notified the public that a data breach involving a third-party technology provider exposed more than 1 million email addresses tied to an online administrative services platform.

According to a statement published by the government of Japan’s third-largest city, hackers accessed the Arara email distribution service used by TKC Corporation , the company contracted to maintain the administrative services platform.

Anyone who received an email from the system run by the city between July 2026 and October 31 had their email address leaked, according to the city. They warned the city’s 2.8 million residents to be wary of suspicious emails purporting to come from the city — urging everyone not to open any URLs or attachments.

The city breach came days after the regional government of the Osaka Prefecture announced its own data breach involving the information of food support program participants.

The attack on Arara has had a cascading effect on dozens of large businesses and governments in Japan. The company said a November 2 cyberattack exposed 77 million email addresses from nearly 400 customers, including TKC, gaming giant Sega and others.

Arara noted that hackers used their email distribution service to send millions of malicious emails pretending to be credit card companies and financial institutions.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Security Affairs.

International law enforcement disrupts Gootloader, seizing domains and taking down over 100 servers linked to 25,000 infected computers. The U.S. Department of Justice announced that law enforcement has removed Gootloader malware from more than 100 computer servers, seized U.S. domain names used to deliver and control it, and notified victims worldwide. “The Department of Justice today announced the successful removal of malware known as “Gootloader” from over 100 computer servers, including compromised WordPress sites, and the seizure of U.S. domain names used by criminals to deliver and control the Gootloader malware. Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Open source hacking tool Artex "significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours," the FBI said.

Open-source AI platform Artex is being used prolifically by cybercriminals and nation-states to breach government agencies and dozens of critical sectors worldwide, according to a new FBI advisory.

The FBI released a flash alert on Friday about the tool, which has caused alarm among cybersecurity experts for its ability to take any large language model and turn it into a powerful hacking tool that can “automate multiple phases of cyber intrusions at machine speed, from reconnaissance through data exfiltration.”

“Artex significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours,” the FBI said. “The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale.”

The tool was released in August on GitHub by an account known as "Autumn-27.” The developer of the framework — identified as Chinese cybersecurity engineer Li Puhua — released a statement on GitHub on October 8 saying the tool was abused by malicious actors.

The developer denied any responsibility for crimes committed with it and eventually removed the GitHub repository.

The FBI said on Friday that despite the removal, the framework “continues to proliferate through community forks, localized variations, archived copies, and a commercial version … ensuring continued availability to threat actors.”

Signal de veille — The Record.

The New York City government will be able to fine companies $1,000 for each verified instance of surveillance pricing.

The New York City Council has approved a bill barring retailers and other businesses from using surveillance pricing to harness customers’ personal data as a means of charging different people variable amounts for the same product.

The metropolis is the second city in the country to pass legislation banning surveillance pricing, following Seattle, where a similar ban was signed into law last month.

The New York City Council voted 44-5 on Thursday in favor of the bill and Mayor Zohran Mamdani celebrated its passage, telling the media “when corporations use your personal data to decide what you pay, you only stand to lose.”

The bill is a “big deal for a few reasons,” according to Grace Gedye, a Consumer Reports policy analyst who worked on the effort to push it through.

“Once this bill becomes law and goes into effect, it will mean eight million fewer people will have to guess about whether their search history, what they are hovering over online, and more, is shaping the price they see,” Gedye said via email.

“It also means a lot of businesses may need to change their pricing practices — and if they already have to do it for New York City, they may decide to do it for the rest of the country at the same time.”

In the biggest overhaul of the country’s spy laws of the postwar era, the Bundestag approved the bill by 308 votes to 190 — with 71 abstentions — months after Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s cabinet signed off on the draft.

German lawmakers passed legislation Friday allowing the country’s intelligence agencies to hack foreign systems, sabotage adversaries’ supply chains and take down servers run by hostile state-backed hackers.

In the biggest overhaul of the country’s spy laws of the postwar era, the Bundestag approved the bill by 308 votes to 190 — with 71 abstentions — months after Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s cabinet signed off on the draft.

At the time the powers were proposed, Chancellery chief Nina Warken said they could allow the nation’s agencies to use cyber operations to sabotage drone factories or chemical weapons laboratories and to disable servers run by hostile state-sponsored hackers.

Intelligence reform is a sensitive subject in Germany, where the shadows cast by both the Gestapo and Stasi remain within living memory. But, as with the country’s increased military spending following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the government has pointed to a rapidly changing threat environment to justify the legislation.

Germany’s Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called the bill the “reform of the century” during the Bundestag debate, saying the new powers would turn the country’s agencies into “genuine intelligence services” operating “on equal footing with our European partners.”

Signal de veille — Silicon.fr.

Microsoft 365 en panne : la France reste touchée

La panne mondiale de Microsoft 365 perturbe toujours Outlook en France, malgré une reprise partielle annoncée par Microsoft.

Microsoft a confirmé une reprise partielle dans certaines régions, mais celle-ci n’est pas encore jugée durable.

L’incident a commencé jeudi, peu avant 19 heures, heure de Paris. En l’espace d’environ une heure, les signalements se sont multipliés dans les Amériques, en Europe, en Asie-Pacifique et en Afrique. Selon Downdetector , la perturbation a été observée dans 74 pays et territoires.

Les services Exchange Online, qui assurent l’hébergement et l’acheminement des e-mails pour de nombreuses organisations, sont au cœur du problème.

En France, les difficultés concernent l’accès à Outlook, la réception et l’envoi de messages, ainsi que la connexion aux services Microsoft 365. La situation reste toutefois moins documentée en volume que celle observée aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, en Inde ou dans plusieurs pays d’Asie-Pacifique.

Microsoft ne communique pas, à ce stade, de répartition précise des utilisateurs affectés par pays. Il est donc impossible d’affirmer que la France est l’une des régions les plus touchées.
